title: Clause triage pocket guide (personal notes)
content:
Purpose: quick pocket reference for triaging contract clauses during sales/negotations. Use this when reviewing first redline or prepping quick guidance for AE/SE. Not canonical legal advice — capture questions for LGL/Procurement.

TL;DR triage rubric (1-5) — how to prioritize ask/escalation:
- 1 (cosmetic): phrasing, boilerplate wordsmithing. No deal impact. Low attention.
- 2 (minor risk): clarifications, sequencing, non-material timelines. Handle with template language.
- 3 (moderate): financial exposure or operational friction (narrow audit rights, modest indemnities, non-standard termination). Needs legal review.
- 4 (high): caps on liability, IP ownership push, data residency demands, cross-border data transfers, broad indemnities, customer wants to host weights. Escalate to LGL lead.
- 5 (deal breaker): unlimited indemnity, broad PII sale/processing exceptions, export control conflicts, binding arbitration in hostile jurisdiction, anything that contradicts SOC/Security attestations or our SLA hard promises. Stop-sign — require exec/legal signoff.

Quick clause checklist (what I scan first, in priority order):
1) Liability / Cap / Consequential damages — do we have a clear cap tied to fees? If customer asks for unlimited liability, set to 3rd-party breach carveouts and push cap to committed spend or 12 months revenue.
   - Ask: "Liability cap = monthly committed fees x12; exclude IP indemnity and willful misconduct."
   - Fallback: "Cap = aggregate fees in prior 12 months."
2) Indemnity — who indemnifies for model outputs? We don't accept broad output-based indemnities. Narrow to: breach of contract, IP infringement (limited to our deliverables), gross negligence, willful misconduct.
   - Script: "We can indemnify for direct infringement claims related to the model we ship; cannot accept indemnity for customer use of generated content."
3) Data handling & PII — data controller/processor callouts, DPA, security controls, deletion/return timelines. Ensure DPA attached, subprocessors disclosure, breach notification <=72 hours.
   - Hot flags: customer demands deletion of model weights or persistent KV store wipe beyond our retention policies.
4) Audit rights — prefer remote evidence vs on-site audits. Limit frequency (1/yr) and scope to security posture. Put confidentiality + redaction obligations.
5) SLA & credits — ensure SLOs map to product offering (hosted vs dedicated vs private). Do not promise hard latency SLAs unless product/infra commit exists.
6) Termination and transition assistance — ask for reasonable handover fees/time; avoid open-ended obligations that require indefinite support after termination.
7) Subprocessors / subcontractors / hosting — require notice and opt-out only for high-risk subprocessors. For private deployments, confirm customer-managed infra exceptions.
8) Export control / sanctions — ensure customer is not sanctioned party; include standard warranty.
9) IP & model weights — never transfer model weights unless explicit commercial agreement (rare). If asked, route to Product + Legal, add commercial terms and security review.
10) Confidentiality & publicity — standard NDA language fine; push back on customer unilateral publicity or benchmark claims without approval.

Sample short redline phrases I keep using:
- Liability cap: "Aggregate liability shall not exceed the total fees paid by Customer to Redwood in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim."
- Data breach notice: "Redwood will notify Customer without undue delay and in any event within seventy-two (72) hours after becoming aware of a Confirmed Security Incident."
- Subprocessor notice: "Redwood will provide Customer with prior written notice of any new Subprocessor and allow Customer thirty (30) days to raise security objections."
- Model outputs indemnity carve: "Customer shall indemnify Redwood for claims arising from Customer's use of generated outputs, except to the extent caused by Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct."

Escalation triggers (immediate legal lead ping + AE pause):
- Customer asks for unlimited or uncapped liability.
- Customer requires transfer/escrow of model weights or claims ownership of weights.
- Indemnity tied to generated content without carveouts.
- Data residency demand we cannot meet (e.g., on-prem only in non-supported country).
- Audit asks >1/year, on-site with access to source code.
- SLAs that promise latency numbers in hosted API where we have no formal SLA.

Questions to capture for LGL review (quick template to fill and attach to ticket):
- Who is the counterparty and what product is in scope (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)?
- What is the customer's requested liability cap / indemnity language?
- Is there any data residency or export control ask?
- Are they asking for weights/IP transfer or broad output indemnity?
- Any regulatory sector (finance/health/government) that requires special handling?

Communication playbook for Sales/BizDev (what to tell customer today):
- Be explicit about what we can do: "We can commit to commercially reasonable security and a DPA; our liability cap is tied to fees; we cannot accept output-based indemnities without very narrow limits."
- If customer pushes: "We'll need to run this by Legal — may require a limited carveout, commercial credit, or additional support fees."
- For dedicated/private asks: "There are configuration and security tradeoffs; we typically treat these with a dedicated SOW and implementation timeline."

Quick running notes / TODOs (personal):
- Update template DPA with 72h breach window and subprocessors clause (open task in JIRA LEG-837).
- Confirm with Infra/SRE what SLA numbers are supportable for Dedicated tier (latency P50/P95 targets).
- Draft 2–3 one-liners for AE playbook: short "we can/cannot" answers.
- Keep a copy of recent negotiated caps: ACME (cap = 1x ARR), Beacon (cap = 12 months fees), for precedent.

Examples of negotiation language (one-liners to copy-paste for AE):
- "We propose a mutual limitation of liability, capped at the greater of twelve (12) months of fees or $1,000,000, excluding liability for willful misconduct."
- "We can agree to on-site audit only for scope limited to security controls and with 30 days notice; Redwood may redact proprietary materials."

Notes to self: watch for creeping obligations in SOWs — sometimes operational commitments migrate into Master Agreement quietly. Always cross-check SOW performance commitments against SLA + infra capabilities.

Slack/Jira sources I reference frequently:
- #legal-deals thread for precedent and current ask.
- JIRA LEG-837 (DPA refresh), JIRA OPS-222 (Dedicated SLA numbers).

Finish checklist before sending redline back:
- Fill escalation template and tag LEG lead.
- Attach product/pricing sheet (to check fee basis for cap).
- Add fallback commercial concessions (eg: additional support fee, warranty period) so AE can offer tradeoffs.

Random notes / open questions to follow up with Marcus: what is current stance on output-based indemnities for open-source models? Product has been inconsistent.

Bottom line (for quick glance):
- Liability/indemnity/data/weights = high priority.
- SLA/termination/audit = medium.
- Boilerplate/wording = low.

End of notes.
